# TSMP Core 1.0.0

Stable release of Trans Sync Media Protocol. This release includes every feature, fix and optimization shipped in the 0.3.0 betas since stable 0.2.0; it is not only a version bump of the last beta's release notes.

## Changes Since 0.2.0

This section consolidates **0.3.0-beta.1, 0.3.0-beta.2 and 0.3.0-beta.3**, not just the final beta.

### TransSync Sending and Component Controls

- Implement per-field `Priority`, `SendOnChange` and `MinSendInterval` in both native Unity and Udon. Compare serialized contents, including mutations to existing arrays, and measure intervals from successful output.
- Send higher-priority fields first, rotate equal-priority fields after successful output, reserve queued RPC capacity before automatic variables and defer fields that do not fit without truncating them.
- Add unchanged-value refresh, defaulting to one second. A zero `transSyncRefreshInterval` disables refresh. Preserve pending state on failure; when no data is eligible, preserve the last output and frame index.
- Add the shared Inspector **Send Mode** dropdown: Default uses each field's attribute, On Change enables filtering with refresh, and Always also sends unchanged values. Changes apply live without rebuilding bindings. Eligibility, minimum intervals, priority and capacity still apply; RPCs and manual Writer calls are unaffected.
- Add opt-in `TransSync.SentEvent` so avatar root delta and keepalive state commit only after successful output. Guard against encoder reentry during callbacks.

### Timeline, Animator, BlendShapes and Avatars

- Apply the first Timeline position independently of the drift threshold, prepare paused graphs before evaluating, and avoid rebuilding stopped graphs for repeated packets.
- Implement Continuous Timeline drift correction, including the shortest correction across loop boundaries. Clear pending corrections when reception is disabled, the component is disabled or the Director changes.
- Reject malformed Timeline packets, unknown states and invalid times before applying them; clear outgoing data when the source is unavailable.
- Fix Play/Resume after Stop without restarting an already playing Director. Add `Seek(float)` with playback-state preservation and local duration bounds.
- Respect receiver Animator layer selection, correct drift across looping/non-looping states, and read negative state hashes without Udon conversion failures.
- Invalidate stale BlendShape interpolation targets when selections, Renderer, mesh or receive state changes.
- Ignore TransSync reception before decoding field values for Receive Interpolation None. Clear pending Rigidbody velocities when physics reception is disabled.
- Deactivate avatar pool slots above a reduced Max Players limit and clear retired assignments. Retain their objects/rigs for reuse; do not destroy supplied pool objects. Pool Size includes retained inactive objects.

### Decoder Consistency, Ordering and Throughput

- Capture a private image so header, calibration and payload use the same source even when the live input changes during readback. Cancel pending results after disable and release owned resources.
- Filter duplicate and older frames with wrap-aware UInt32 ordering. Add receiver-local **Window Size**, default 256: frame zero may restart ordering when the previous applied index reaches one window.
- Reuse payload capacity across shorter frames while bounding parsing and diagnostics to valid bytes. Reject empty/truncated NetworkFrame payloads before payload readback. Keep exact-length plugin arguments and independent received field arrays.
- Add the default-enabled predicted path: use the previous validated configuration to decode the **current** header and payload in one GPU readback. Always validate the current header CRC. Equal length never means reusing old payload contents.
- Fall back on the same frozen image when codec, options, stream, layout, sample size or payload length changes. Require an exact payload-length match; custom codecs are not assumed to support arbitrary prefix decoding.
- Keep manual layout and safety modes on the sequential path; retain sequential fallback when prediction resources are unavailable. Add advanced opt-outs and prediction/fallback diagnostics.
- Overlap at most two independent captures and apply results in capture order. Full slots skip new captures instead of building an unbounded queue; cancellation drains outstanding requests before buffer reuse. Add an overlap opt-out and pending/busy-capture diagnostics.
- Let opted-in codec shaders write header and payload bytes directly to the readback texture, removing a payload intermediate and packing draw. Existing third-party shaders retain the legacy path.

### CPU, GPU and Memory

- Replace same-type Udon image/payload loops with guarded bulk copies, preserving receiver and in-flight buffer isolation.
- Read GPU output into slot-owned byte arrays and bulk-copy validated ranges without retaining request-owned native views.
- Reuse encoder-owned native raster storage through an optional codec API, keeping the original writer fallback.
- Match known 8-bit/half-float snapshot formats and linear/sRGB interpretation. Keep Float32 for unknown/high-precision inputs and non-RenderTexture Udon sources.
- Encode Luma4 bytes into a small GPU symbol image before block expansion. Prepare materials automatically, retain CPU fallback, defer unused CPU image allocation and release owned GPU resources. Native codecs explicitly opt in.
- Add `TSMPCodec.PrepareDecode(Texture, Material)`, `GetDecodeSampleSize`, calibration-LUT helpers and the optional `calibrationMaterial`. Codecs own Float32 LUT allocation, per-pass refresh and cleanup; Core does not select codec-specific algorithms.
- Remove Setup's redundant Editor output Blit. Only successful Encoder output is presented.
- Preserve integer pixel blocks during expansion and clear right/bottom remainders when dimensions are not divisible by block size.

### RPC and Desktop Streaming

- Preserve RPC queue accounting under reentrant sends and reject events that can never fit the configured payload. Repeats remain a finite attempt budget, not acknowledged delivery.
- Reject FFmpeg source/output dimension mismatches before startup and stop publishing when source dimensions change. Validate RGBA32 readbacks before flipping/writing; do not silently resize TSMP pixels.
- Isolate processes, buffers, callbacks and diagnostics per FFmpeg session so stopped sessions cannot submit into restarted sessions.
- Use cooperative writer shutdown and terminate blocked processes, dispose resources after the writer finishes, detect unexpected exits and restore background execution on failure/shutdown.
- Pace FFmpeg output independently of texture updates while retaining the latest frame.

### Documentation and Regression Coverage

- Update English, Korean and Japanese sending, decoding, codec API, shader integration and installation guides.
- Add reusable English issue templates and contribution guidance across the repositories.
- Add native/Udon scheduling and Timeline regression tests, FFmpeg lifecycle cases, changing-source decoder tests, GPU pixel comparisons and repeatable Player/Udon performance and delivery measurements.

## Update and Compatibility

| Package | Stable version |
| --- | --- |
| TSMP Core | 1.0.0 |
| Luma4 | 1.0.0 |
| RGB16 | 2.0.0 |
| RGB20 | 2.0.0 |
| Color256 | 2.0.0 |

- VCC: use https://vpm.kiba.red/ and install the stable versions. Prerelease visibility is no longer required. Codec UPM dependencies specify Core 1.0.0; VPM accepts Core >=1.0.0. Update Core and the installed codecs together.
- Ordinary Unity: install Core and Luma4 (plus any chosen codec) through UPM using their extracted package.json files or explicit package sources. VRCSDK is not required. Package metadata does not make UPM fetch these packages from GitHub automatically.
- VRChat Worlds SDK remains a VPM-only dependency, >=3.9.0. Both environments use the same Controller and automatic setup. Allow Unity to refresh bindings and recompile UdonSharp after updating.
- **Sending changes since 0.2.0:** SendOnChange now affects traffic. For continuous resend, select Send Mode Always; for custom fields, use `SendOnChange = false, MinSendInterval = 0`. Always does not override intervals/capacity or guarantee delivery. Strict priority can starve lower-priority fields under overload.
- **Receiving changes:** duplicate filtering now includes older frames. Window Size is a restart heuristic, not a session ID. Delayed old zero frames, lost reset frames, early restarts and high old frame indices after a reset remain ambiguous. Switching streams replaces the successful-application baseline; there is no retired-stream history.
- Prediction, overlap, combined output and GPU Luma4 have advanced opt-outs/fallbacks. Two-slot overlap trades extra storage/work and potentially higher latency for capture throughput; it is not a lossless transport.
- Use `TSMPEncoder.output` as the authoritative encoded image. The hidden `outputTexture` is CPU staging and is not refreshed by GPU encoding.
- Existing custom codecs can retain their original writer/shader paths and no-op preparation. New package sources require Core 1.0.0; a missing preparation material cannot compensate for an older Core API.
- FFmpeg remains native desktop functionality, not an Udon process inside VRChat. Restart it after changing session dimensions/frame rate; YUV420p needs even dimensions.
- In Udon, control Timeline through the sync component; directly controlling the Director externally and detecting automatic completion remain limited by exposed Udon APIs.
- Existing script/material/prefab GUIDs are preserved. The stable promotion changes release metadata/docs, not the runtime or shaders from the latest betas. The three optional codecs use 2.0.0 so their historical 1.0.0 tags/releases remain intact.

## Datagram

The protocol version and wire bytes remain unchanged: **56-byte header, followed by the existing payload**. No session, window, scheduling or overlap fields are added.

| Byte range | Field | Encoding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 20..23 | StreamId | UInt32 little-endian |
| 24..27 | FrameIndex | UInt32 little-endian |
| 28..31 | TimestampMs | UInt32 little-endian; not used for ordering |
| 44..49 | Reserved | Six zero bytes |
| 52..55 | Header CRC32 | UInt32 little-endian over bytes 0..51 |

Window Size is receiver-local. Codec IDs, packet layouts, CRC validation, finite RPC repeats and RPC event deduplication are preserved.

## Measured Improvements

These are the measurements obtained during the included betas, **not a new 0.2.0-versus-1.0.0 benchmark**. The resource baseline is Core b80194c, already containing predicted/two-slot decoding.

Unity 2022.3.22f1; Windows 11; i9-13900K; RTX 4090; D3D11; Luma4, block size 8, sample size 1. One always-sent byte-array field, three-second warmup and twelve-second measurement. Udon uses Worlds 3.10.4-beta.2's SDK Editor VM after a full client-target compile. Native uses a Windows x64 Development Mono Player with stripping disabled.

| Measurement | Before | After | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Udon encoder, 720p / 4 KiB / 60 Hz, mean | 11.27 ms | 0.457 ms | 24.7x faster |
| Udon decoder submission + callback means | 3.904 ms | 0.791 ms | 4.9x faster |
| Udon send + receive root means | 15.17 ms | 1.248 ms | 91.8% less CPU time |
| Native publish, 720p / 4 KiB, mean | 3.33 ms | 0.095 ms | 97.1% less CPU time |
| Native publish, 4K / 32 B, mean | 20.72 ms | 0.141 ms | 99.3% less CPU time |
| Whole-Player median frame GC allocation, native 720p | 3,686,964 B | 612 B | 99.98% lower |
| Two 8-bit snapshots, 720p, texel storage | 28.13 MiB | 7.03 MiB | 75% smaller |
| Two 8-bit snapshots, 4K, texel storage | 253.13 MiB | 63.28 MiB | 75% smaller |

The summed means are CPU work, **not end-to-end latency** or a measured frame-time percentile. They exclude avatar capture, IK, interpolation, streaming and world rendering. Encoder p95 was 0.546 ms; callback p95 was 0.495 ms. Allocation counters cover the whole Player; collections/startup spikes still occurred. Snapshot savings are not total RAM/VRAM savings.

Small payloads also benefited: Udon raster CPU time fell from 0.158 to 0.066 ms at 360p / 32 B and from 0.200 to 0.064 ms at 4K / 32 B.

GPU tradeoff: Luma4 adds a conversion draw. Gamma conversion/expansion medians were about 16.5 us versus 8.3 us at 720p, and 93.8 us versus 81.0 us at 4K, excluding upload/readback/world rendering. This is not a universal GPU speedup.

## Delivery, Validation and Limits

- Final native/Udon profiles received 361/361 published frames at 30 Hz and 721/721 at 60 Hz in the measured cases. The 4K small-payload Udon case sustained about 30 Hz instead of 23.53 Hz.
- A separate automatic-scheduling test capped at 30 FPS received 1799/1799 frames over 60 seconds in both two-slot runs. One-slot controls received 1579/1800 (native) and 1758/1800 (Udon). Median application latency increased from about 33.3 to 66.6 ms.
- A 30-FPS receiver cannot capture every independently changing 60-FPS source image. Finite local tests do not guarantee lossless OBS/video/network transport.
- Included beta validation passed native scheduling/Timeline tests, 13 FFmpeg lifecycle cases, actual Transform/Humanoid/Timeline/Unicode/RPC texture loopback in a Windows Mono Player, full client-target UdonSharp compilation, SDK VM tests and a local SDK world bundle build.
- Later suites passed 216 changing-source decoder cases, native Gamma/Linear and compiled Udon GPU/CPU pixel comparisons, codec/payload switching, CRC rejection, source overwrite, independent receivers, ordered completion, disable/re-enable, fallback and RPC deduplication.
- Public beta ZIPs matched release-tag contents and VPM hashes. Fresh-project Windows Player and 24-script Udon compilation/VM tests passed. Initial SDK bootstrap class/cache errors and successful reopen/confirmation runs are recorded, not hidden.
- **Not verified:** uploaded/live VRChat, Quest/mobile, other GPUs/APIs, IL2CPP/managed stripping, OBS/MediaMTX transport, populated avatar scenes or long soaks. The full legacy Linear loopback harness had a CPU calibration/block-expansion failure; separate passing Linear pixel/decoder tests do not certify that older harness. Existing shader warnings remain.

## Stable Artifact Verification

The public stable ZIPs were checked against release tags and VPM hashes, then tested in fresh SDK-free and SDK projects. The Windows Mono Player passed; after SDK initialization, full 24-script UdonSharp compilation and compiled VM regression passed on two launches. Initial SDK class/cache errors and all validation limits are retained in the [stable verification record](https://github.com/kibalab/TSMP-Core/blob/main/Validation~/PackageCompatibility/STABLE-20260919.md). This post-publication check does not change the tagged package contents or introduce new performance measurements.
